title: Purim: the feast and gifts
hookLine: two food gifts, gifts to two poor people, and a joyful meal
tomorrow: Saba says Passover cleaning means scrubbing the walls. does it?

lines: FEASTING, PORTIONS, GIFTS TO THE POOR.
WHY SEND YOU OUT THE DOOR?
cards: Most parties come with a guest list. This one comes with a delivery list. The Book of Esther says the days are to be "days of feasting and gladness, and of sending portions one to another, and gifts to the poor."
A feast, yes. But also food carried to friends, and gifts carried to strangers. Why would a day of joy send you out the door to people you may not even know?

teach.b: The Talmud reads the plurals closely. Portions, one to another: at least two foods to one friend, called mishloach manot.

teach.h: A GIFT EACH TO TWO IN NEED.
teach.b: Gifts to the poor: a gift each to at least two people in need. Then the meal, the seudah, later in the day. Maimonides weighs the three and comes down clearly.

Better to spend more on gifts to the poor than on the feast or the portions, because there is no greater and more glorious joy than gladdening the hearts of the poor, the orphans, the widows and the strangers.
So the joy of Purim travels outward: from the table, to a friend's door, to someone who has less. Now hold up the last six days together. Ordinary is holy too: Hillel's bath.

teach.h: SIX LINES, PLAIN MONTH TO FEAST.
teach.b: Light in the window: lit for the street. Coins of light: some for play, some so another window glows. Fast with meaning: a meal's cost to the hungry.
Plant something: Honi's carob. Hear it all: every word of the scroll. From a plain month to a feast, six lines.

how: On Purim day, Jews send mishloach manot, a gift of at least two ready-to-eat foods, to at least one friend, give gifts of money or food to at least two people in need, and hold a festive meal, the seudah, in the afternoon.

practice: For the sit, plan one food gift. Who gets it: a neighbor, a friend, someone who had a hard winter? What two things go in it: a piece of fruit, something baked, anything ready to eat?
And one gift for someone in need, however small. Hold both faces in mind while the time runs.
